reason: The canonical assertion is itself the specified signed-kernel counterexample. All its clauses are present: evenness, integrability, mass one, one-point translate identity, negative integral, strict decrease, the continuous triangular population, its exact negative interval at zero, and almost-sure CDF-domain and real-square-root failure for every positive sample size. The fixed square-root functional is a well-defined map on the CDF domain; failure to belong to that domain, together with absence of a real square root, supplies its claimed failure without evaluating Lean's total Real.sqrt at a negative number. IID samples with the triangular common law exist on the countable product probability space.

For every positive sample size, real tuple, a.e. nonnegative even normalized kernel, and positive bandwidth, the theorem states every specified density and CDF property. Monotonicity and the endpoint limits imply the CDF range bounds; continuity implies right continuity. Consequently the function lies in the domain of every statistical functional on CDFs, as claimed. The integral-equals-one assumption excludes Bochner's nonintegrable default zero; no extra integrability restriction or hidden conclusion hypothesis is present.

The defined integrated estimator uses the corrected kernel-density integrand. The theorem gives exactly the change-of-variables formula for every integrable kernel and the rectangular-density empirical-CDF difference, with exactly the printed proviso that no observation equals the lower endpoint x-h. Positive sizes and bandwidths exclude zero division. Its deterministic quantification covers all IID realizations and its first clause harmlessly also covers unnormalized or nonsymmetric integrable kernels.

The canonical assertion is the heavy-tail counterexample, not the positive bootstrap claim quoted within it. The mixture, survival formula, local CDF, unique median, tail thresholds, odd-median marginal and conditional Gaussian limits, and uniform variance obstruction are present. The specified T0 is evaluated on empirical CDFs at all positive sizes, has the stated unrestricted bounded-direction Hadamard derivative, has both all-size weak limits, and has the stated odd-size obstruction and all-size nonconvergence. Constant-label outcomes have probability n^(-n) under independently uniform label draws, so the witness respects the printed bootstrap design. All conditional moments used are finite for each sample; no unconditional finite-sample estimator variance is required by this canonical assertion.

The root-n marginal Gaussian premise, positive phi, exact n-out-of-n conditional weak-bootstrap premise, real-cutoff square-tail criterion, variance equivalence, and explicitly conditional standard-deviation conclusion match the canonical statement. The sample-mean identity and positive-finite-variance consistency, and the all-positive-size median case with a local positive density and a positive-order absolute moment, are retained. Composite measurability of observed and resampled statistics is a usual measure-theoretic condition, not a substantive extra restriction. The limsup is of probabilities bounded in [0,1], not of possibly unbounded moments. Both formerly ambiguous docstrings now explicitly condition the standard-deviation conclusion on the equivalent moment/variance conditions.
